fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: A knocked-out tooth is one of the most time-sensitive dental emergencies. The sooner an adult tooth is placed back into its socket, the better its chances of survival. If this has just happened, stay calm, follow the steps below and call us immediately on {{site:phone}}.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Is a Knocked-Out Tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A knocked-out tooth, also called an avulsed tooth, is a tooth that has been completely dislodged from its socket, usually as the result of a fall, a sporting injury or an accident. When a tooth is knocked out, the delicate cells on the root surface begin to dry out and die, which is why acting quickly is so important.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Teeth can also be partially dislodged, pushed out of position or pushed further into the gum. These injuries need prompt care too.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: When to Seek Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A knocked-out adult tooth needs urgent dental attention, ideally within 30 minutes. Call us straight away.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Baby teeth are handled differently. A knocked-out baby tooth should not be put back in, as this can damage the developing adult tooth beneath. Please see our children's dental emergencies page and contact us for advice.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: If the injury involves a blow to the head, loss of consciousness, uncontrolled bleeding or a suspected jaw fracture, call 000 or go to your nearest hospital emergency department first.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Find the tooth and pick it up by the crown, the white part you usually see, avoiding touching the root.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: If the tooth is dirty, rinse it briefly in milk or saline. Do not scrub the root.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: If possible, gently push the tooth back into its socket, making sure it faces the right way, then bite on a clean cloth or handkerchief to hold it in place.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: If you cannot replant it, store the tooth in a small container of milk, or hold it in your mouth between your cheek and gum. Do not wrap it in tissue or let it dry out.

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Call us immediately and come straight to the practice.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We examine the tooth and surrounding area and take digital X-rays to check the socket, root and neighbouring teeth. If the tooth has been replanted, we check its position. If not, we clean the area and gently reposition the tooth. A flexible splint is usually bonded to the neighbouring teeth to hold the tooth steady while it heals. We also check for soft tissue injuries to the lips, gums and tongue. Depending on the injury, root canal therapy is often recommended within the following weeks, and we may advise a tetanus check with your GP.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Eat soft foods, avoid biting with the injured tooth, and keep the area clean with gentle brushing and any mouth rinse we recommend. The splint is usually removed after a few weeks. Regular reviews over the following months and years are important, as complications can develop over time. If the tooth cannot be saved, we will discuss replacement options such as dental implants. Wearing a custom mouthguard during sport can help reduce the risk of future injuries.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for a Knocked-Out Tooth

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for a Knocked-Out Tooth

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Our central Fortitude Valley location, free on-site parking and dedicated urgent appointment times help you get care quickly. We use digital X-rays to assess injuries accurately and provide clear, calm guidance at every step.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How long do I have to save a knocked-out tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The best outcomes occur when a tooth is replanted within 30 minutes. However, seek care even if more time has passed.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Should I put a baby tooth back in?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Replanting a baby tooth can damage the adult tooth developing underneath. Contact us for advice instead.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I store the tooth in water?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Water is not recommended for storage. Milk or saliva helps protect the root cells until you reach us.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will the tooth survive?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Outcomes vary depending on how quickly the tooth is replanted, how it was stored and the extent of the injury. Some teeth need further treatment in future.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Do I need root canal therapy after replanting?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Root canal therapy is often required for adult teeth that have been knocked out, particularly when the root was fully formed.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How can I prevent this from happening again?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A custom-fitted mouthguard is recommended for contact and ball sports to help protect your teeth.
